pr_title: [frontend] isolate api server process and engine process
pr_body:
fix the bug reported in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/6152#issuecomment-2282998308 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/7151#issuecomment-2282985736

both of them are using minicpmv model https://huggingface.co/openbmb/MiniCPM-V-2_6 

the root cause, turns out to be:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/86ab567bae0698425095e28cce67e9a31a261b72/vllm/entrypoints/openai/api_server.py#L63-L69

when huggingface use `AutoConfig` to load the config, the model class module can happen to initialize cuda, when it imports some modules.

this pr tries to fix the problem, by isolating the api server process and engine process.

before this pr, engine process is a fork of the api server process.

after this pr, they are separated into different processes.

thanks for @HwwwwwwwH to help find out the root cause.

might also fix https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/7246 

@LSC527 would you mind testing it?
I've tested the code of this PR and it worked fine.

@youkaichao can't we just switch to use spawn here? You can have separate multiprocessing contexts, it doesn't need to affect what we're doing with the back-end distributed inference multiprocessing (that already uses a dedicated mp context).
I can see how the `ModelConfig` could be causing issues, but I don't think this could be the root cause #6152 and #7151 since those are on versions from before we introduced multiprocessing

@njhill `spawn` might be another option, but it will require users' code with explicit `if __name__ == "__main__"` .This works fine for the api server currently, but can cause trouble in the future when we further isolate the user-facing process and the engine process in offline batching inference.

@robertgshaw2-neuralmagic #7151 is an old issue, that is solved by `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn` . My investigation starts from the specific comment https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/7151#issuecomment-2282985736 , that uses 0.5.4 and `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn` does not work.

> @robertgshaw2-neuralmagic #7151 is an old issue, that is solved by `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn` . My investigation starts from the specific comment [#7151 (comment)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/7151#issuecomment-2282985736) , that uses 0.5.4 and `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn` does not work.

I see. That makes sense!

> @njhill `spawn` might be another option, but it will require users' code with explicit `if __name__ == "__main__"` .This works fine for the api server currently, but can cause trouble in the future when we further isolate the user-facing process and the engine process in offline batching inference.

But this isn't user code right? Can't we just also include that in our entrypoints? Would kind of prefer the simpler option unless/until we need to do something different...

this PR is closed in favor of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/7484 .

I left the diff here, in case we need it in the future.
